title: Supplier bale and carton quantities
captions: Procure Flow now helps you request quantities that suppliers can fulfil as
full bales or cartons. The selected supplier's pack size follows the request
through approval, purchasing and receiving. Here's how to use it.

title: Check the selected supplier
captions: Start in Create Request, or select a supplier offer from Supplier Stock.
Confirm the supplier and product, then check the bale or carton size
shown for that item. Another supplier may use a different pack size.

title: Quantities round up to a full pack
captions: With thirty units per pack, entering thirty one adjusts the request to
sixty when you leave the quantity field.
The adjustment message explains the change.
Plus and minus controls move by one full pack.
Review the new quantity and recalculated totals.

title: Review drafts before submitting
captions: Check the receiving site, each line's need by date, price and total.
Save Draft keeps your work for later.
If an older draft contains an odd quantity, correct it to a
full pack before saving or submitting.
Follow the existing approval and Concur handover.

title: Resolve an unconfirmed pack
captions: If the bale or carton size is unconfirmed, new ordering is blocked.
Ask Procurement to confirm the supplier pack data, then refresh and try
again. Do not guess a size.
A supplier confirmed pack of one allows loose units.

title: Pack details stay with the order
captions: Open Request Details to see the saved pack size and number of
full packs. These details remain with the order when supplier data changes
later. Finance and line reports retain the same context.
Older orders with no recorded pack are labelled as legacy.

title: Receive the actual quantity delivered
captions: In Record Delivery, enter the units actually delivered, even when a carton
is incomplete. A delivery of seven units stays seven.
Use Add Unplanned Item for goods outside the original order, and follow
the existing variance process.

title: Check the quantity before ordering
captions: Before submitting, confirm the supplier, pack size, adjusted quantity and total.
During receiving, record actual units. Pack counts explain the order;
they do not replace unit quantities or prices in Concur.
Use the feature guide whenever you need a reminder.
